title: program.committed
description: A piece of code that builds a circuit now exists. Programs are the unit of evolution — the thing that is mutated, inherited from, and attributed. A program is not yet a result; it becomes one when a candidate.measured event scores it. Subject is prog:<blob>.

blob.description: Digest of the program in the blob store. One blob per program: bundle every file that affects the output (imported modules, data files it reads), not just the entry script. Content-addressed, which means duplicate work deduplicates itself: if two lab assistants independently write identical code, it is one program. This is why the researcher broadcasts a direction rather than assigning tasks — no claiming or locking is needed.

parent.description: WHAT CODE THIS CAME FROM. Digest of the program this was edited from, or null for a root/baseline. Nobody stores the search tree; it is reconstructed by following these links. Use it to find which direction of travel was working, and which branches to stop spending on. Do not confuse with `cause`.

benchmark.description: Which competition task this program targets, e.g. 'invsqrt', 'dqi', 'dfthcsos'. Denormalized onto both program.committed and candidate.measured — technically redundant, kept because it makes nearly every query simpler.

note.description: Optional free text from the author — what was changed and why, one or two sentences. Not validated, not parsed. Useful in digests, since it is far cheaper than diffing source.
